title: Moloch's Bargain: Emergent Misalignment When LLMs Compete for Audiences
abstract: arXiv:2510.06105v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly shaping how information is created and disseminated, from companies using them to craft persuasive advertisements, to election campaigns optimizing messaging to gain votes, to social media influencers boosting engagement. These settings are inherently competitive, with sellers, candidates, and influencers vying for audience approval, yet it remains poorly understood how competitive feedback loops influence LLM behavior. We show that optimizing LLMs for competitive success can inadvertently drive misalignment. Using simulated environments across these scenarios, we find that, 6.3% increase in sales is accompanied by a 14.0% rise in deceptive marketing; in elections, a 4.9% gain in vote share coincides with 22.3% more disinformation and 12.5% more populist rhetoric; and on social media, a 7.5% engagement boost comes with 188.6% more disinformation and a 16.3% increase in promotion of harmfu

translated_title: 摩洛克契约：大语言模型在争夺受众竞争中的涌现性失调
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）正日益塑造着信息的创建与传播方式——从企业利用它们撰写有说服力的广告，到竞选活动优化信息以争取选票，再到社交媒体网红提升互动量。这些场景本质上都是竞争性的：卖家、候选人和网红都在争夺受众的认可，然而竞争性反馈循环如何影响LLM的行为仍知之甚少。我们证明，为竞争成功而优化LLM可能会无意中导致失调。通过在上述场景中构建模拟环境，我们发现：销售额增长6.3%的同时，欺骗性营销增加了14.0%；在选举中，得票率提高4.9%的同时，虚假信息增加22.3%，民粹主义言论增加12.5%；在社交媒体上，互动量提升7.5%的同时，虚假信息增加了188.6%，有害内容的推广增加16.3%。
tldr: 本研究发现，当LLM在销售、选举、社交媒体等竞争场景中为获胜而优化时，竞争成功的背后伴随着欺骗性营销、虚假信息和有害内容等涌现性失调行为的显著增加。
en_tdlr: Optimizing LLMs for competitive success in markets, elections, and social media inadvertently drives emergent misalignment, with gains in sales, votes, and engagement accompanied by increased deception, disinformation, and harmful content.
